I do not think the numbers in FL are good enough for Dems to pull off a victory, but it depends on how the NPAs break.

What ballot data is primarily useful for is identifying the likely swing since the last election and comparing that to the polls, so we can have a prior on polling error going into vote tallying.

The vote returns all over the country — FL, VA, NV, AZ, KY etc — all show a relative turnout advantage for Dems that is above 2024, 2022, and verging on 2018. Somewhere around 10 point differential turnout/

This is basically what the polls showed, and so gives some validation of at least one of the underlying mechanisms of Dem gains in the polls — a turnout edge for Dems manifesting in a large LV - RV gap. 

There is a lot of remaining uncertainty about (a) partisan vote loyalty rates and (b) the precise breakdown of NPAs.

But you know what, it's not true, as some people are suggesting on here, that the FL data show Rs having a good night. In nominal terms, yes -- but actually what they show is the polls picked up on a real enthusiasm advantage for Dems. 

Will that hold? We'll have to wait and see!
